https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4g3.text: Figure caption, Watch: Was Donald Trump smuggled out of Air Force One in a catering truck? By Brandon Drenon Â and Â Bernd Debusmann Jr ,Â White House reporter Published 12 August 2026, 15:32 BST Updated 2 hours ago Two members of US President Donald Trump's cabinet were on a decoy plane that Trump secretly exited before boarding a different flight in Turkey last month, CBS News reports. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent remained aboard what was believed to be Air Force One and didn't join a flight that was provided to Trump over security concerns involving Iran. After Trump entered Air Force One on 8 July with both officials and members of the press, he hid on a catering truck to be clandestinely transported to a military plane. The label "Air Force One" applies to any plane the president is on, but in this case the original craft kept the call signal, becoming a decoy. Image source, Associated Press According to CBS - the BBC's US partner - Rubio and Bessent remained on board the first aircraft to maintain the line of succession in case something happened to Trump. In the event that the president dies or is incapacitated, Vice-President JD Vance would take power, followed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate. The Secretary of State comes next in line, followed by the treasury secretary. Others who stayed on the initial aircraft designated as Air Force One included White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Steven Cheung, the White House's communications director. The second aircraft that flew President Trump out of Ankara also included Pete Hegseth, the defence secretary, according to US media reports. The BBC has contacted the White House for comment. Speaking to reporters on Monday night, Trump said the decision to undertake the deception was made by the US military and the Secret Service, who "wanted me to go in a different flight". The nature of the security threat remains unclear, with Trump providing no specifics, saying only that he gets "a lot of threats". "Any consequential president has a lot of threats," he added. Figure caption, Watch: What is it like to travel on Air Force One with Trump? It is also unclear what the cabinet secretaries and other officials, along with the Air Force members working on the plane, knew of the operation. Members of the press have said they were not aware that they were on a decoy flight. Various ruses, often referred to as "shell games" by Secret Service personnel, are common. Identical versions of the president's heavily armoured limousine, for example, often switch positions in motorcades, as do helicopters transporting the president in the air. More elaborate operations often take place during high-risk trips abroad, and in those cases reporters on Air Force One are typically briefed and asked not to report the movements in real-time. In March 2000, for example, then-President Bill Clinton flew to the Pakistani capital of Islamabad on an unmarked executive jet that landed after a decoy jet with the livery of Air Force One. Ahead of the trip, the White House informed USA Today reporter Susan Page - then the head of the White House Correspondent's Association - of the security arrangements. "They told me about the extraordinary security procedures being taken because of the dangers flying there, including the use of the decoy plane," Page revealed for the first time this week. "Of course, the dangers threatened the journalists covering the trip as well as President Clinton," she said in an interview with the Washington Post. It is also not currently clear what, if any, danger the occupants of the plane carrying Rubio, Bessent, other staff and the White House press pool were in during the Ankara trip. The White House Correspondent's Association has not publicly commented on the incident. Photograph: Pascal Bastien/AP View image in fullscreen Mark Carney and Ursula von der Leyen are like-minded on many important global issues. Photograph: Pascal Bastien/AP This Is Europe World news The EU’s Canada offer is more mood than reality but it could hint at a future geometry for the bloc While Brussels and Ottawa desire a deeper partnership born of Trump-era volatility, ​the EU has no legal framework to accommodate it Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Jon Henley , Europe correspondent Wed 23 Sep 2026 10.30 EDT Last modified on Wed 23 Sep 2026 10.33 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The EU and Canada, Ursula von der Leyen said last week, “see the world with the same eyes”, with shared stances on everything from AI to the climate crisis, the Ukraine war and the unholy chaos unleashed by the current occupant of the White House (OK, she didn’t actually say that last bit. But I like to think she almost certainly thought it.) So, the European Commission president went on, Canada should become “the first associate member of the EU”. In the audience, Mark Carney beamed with delight. The next day, Canada’s prime minister enthusiastically embraced the idea of an “alliance for the future”, to build “collective resilience” through “deep cooperation”. Cue standing ovations, warm handshakes – and a great deal of head-scratching in Brussels and assorted EU capitals. Because “associate membership” of the EU is not, in fact, a thing. Nor, as a Guardian editorial pointed out , is there “any blueprint for what such a thing might involve”. The term was, the editorial argued, “a political hypothesis”, describing “a relationship of intimate strategic alignment with the EU, stopping short of actual membership, in ways that are significant but undefined”. So what exactly are the commission and Canada playing at here, and where might it lead? You can see where they’re coming from. On paper, in a world of unpredictable and increasingly aggressive great powers, it makes perfect sense. For Canada – which already has the Ceta free trade agreement with the EU – the catalyst for even closer cooperation is clearly Donald Trump: incessant tariff threats , an escalating trade war, bullying talk of Canada as the “51st state”, the renaming of Lake Ontario – all have left Ottawa eager to diversify its relations. Aligning with European industrial strategy, working together on defence and AI, and joining EU scientific research and student exchange programmes would offer Canada a reliable counterweight to its all-too-unreliable southern neighbour. (Unsurprisingly, Trump called the tie-up “laughable” , and threatened more tariffs.) For the EU, meanwhile, Canada is a dream partner: a stable, like-minded “middle power” rich in critical minerals, rare earths and – as Carney couldn’t resist noting – good manners. Plus, Canada’s unbridled EU-enthusiasm is a pleasing boost to the bloc’s bruised ego after Iceland’s recent rejection of more EU accession negotiations. There’s only one problem: “associate membership” is not a status in the EU treaties, and creating such a status would mean treaty reform, which member states won’t contemplate. There are things called “association agreements”, such as with Ukraine , Moldova or Georgia, but those are essentially stepping stones to full membership – which Canada can’t aspire to, for the very good reason that it isn’t in Europe. But if “associate member” sounds vaguely familiar, that’s because the EU has been talking about a “second circle” since the days of Jacques Delors : an outer ring of countries bound by shared values, free trade and security cooperation to an inner core of members, but without full voting rights or complete regulatory integration. Emmanuel Macron’s European Political Community is a variation on this theme, and Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz , recently floated “associate member” status for Ukraine. Indeed, non-EU nations in the European Economic Area (EEA) and European Free Trade Association, such as Norway, Iceland or Switzerland, already function as quasi-associate members, enjoying single-market access while being largely “rule-takers”: adopting EU rules without having a vote in Brussels. Writing in the Guardian, Fabian Zuleeg suggested that Canada and Europe actually need more of an “integrated partnership” – a model that leaves single market access to one side, focusing instead on concrete collaboration in areas such as defence, supply chains and EU programmes like Horizon and Erasmus+. Alberto Alemanno, a professor of EU law, noted that a realistic EU-Canada landing zone would have to go further than Ceta and might more resemble the kind of tailored framework of the EU-Swiss relationship. But the real significance of any formal new status, he said, was that it could make the EU “an institutional hub around which other democracies organise strategic autonomy – but without joining the union”. What that might actually look like is anyone’s guess: visa-free work access, shared military procurement, Canadian seats on EU regulatory committees? For the moment, Canada’s hypothetical “associate membership” is more of a mood than a reality: the expressed intent of a democratic bloc and a middle power to deepen ties in the face of mounting global uncertainty. Does it, all the same, hold any hope for Brexit-regretting Britain ? As Jill Rutter of the Institute for Government highlighted, the EU’s sudden willingness to display “institutional imagination” at least shows that the bloc is willing to think about adapting when geopolitical pressures demand. But a new deal for Canada won’t automatically fix the UK’s issues. As Joël Reland of UK in a Changing Europe pointed out, the vagueness of the EU offer to Canada might look promising for the UK. But Canada wants “deep cooperation” without touching single-market rules, and the UK’s main problem is that it is now shut out of that same market. Whatever Canada eventually gets, it’s unlikely to work for the UK. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion A miserable time for Merz View image in fullscreen Friedrich Merz needs to rethink policy in order to stay on top. Photograph: Fabrizio Bensch/Reuters Friedrich Merz is in trouble. A fortnight after the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) swept to a crushing victory in one state election in Saxony-Anhalt, the German chancellor’s centre-right CDU failed to clear the 5% threshold needed to enter the state parliament in another, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. It fared a little better in Berlin, where it was the incumbent, but was still beaten – by a clear five-point margin – by the far-left Die Linke. And the AfD made headway in the capital, too, surging to a double-digit result. The embattled chancellor has vowed to fight on , but faces an uncomfortable choice: revise the unpopular economic reforms he insists are essential, or risk oblivion defending them. Meanwhile, as long as he refuses to step aside and no one is actively seeking to replace him, a volatile and damaging deadlock will reign in Europe’s biggest economy. After 16 months in office, it is becoming increasingly clear – as a Guardian editorial noted – that Merz is “ill-suited for the job” of defending Germany’s democratic future against the far right. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/isr.text: BOMB SCARE: LOT Flight Carrying Jewish Students From London Makes Emergency Landing Outside Warsaw November 3, 2026 3:20 pm No Comments A LOT Polish Airlines flight from London to Warsaw with a group of Jewish and Israeli students on board made an unscheduled landing on Tuesday morning after an emergency report of a bomb on the plane. Flight LO286 had taken off from Heathrow Airport and was headed for Warsaw Chopin Airport when the alert came in at 9:54 AM local time. About seven minutes later, the Boeing 737 MAX touched down at Modlin Airport outside the Polish capital. The plane was immediately sent to an isolated area. The airport was temporarily shut down, and local security forces began a thorough search of the aircraft. There were 181 passengers on board, including a group of Jewish and Israeli students aged 16 to 17 who live in Britain. The passengers were taken off the plane without their personal belongings and brought to a screening area. The mother of one of the students said the passengers were removed without their luggage and sent for security checks, and that they would travel on to Warsaw by bus instead of a connecting flight. The incident is the latest in a series of threats against flights across Europe over the past day. A Scandinavian SAS flight from Copenhagen also received a security threat on Tuesday and landed at Chopin Airport, where the threat was checked without halting the airport’s regular operations. On Monday, a Wizz Air flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Budapest with an escort of Hungarian fighter jets. After a search, it turned out to be a false alarm. The latest wave of threats follows similar incidents last month targeting flights to and from Israel. An Austrian Airlines flight from Ben Gurion Airport to Vienna was forced to land in Bulgaria, and two Delta flights between New York and Tel Aviv were delayed or evacuated after anonymous messages warning of explosives. Beállítom „Kedves Barátaim! 5 hónap után hazatérhettem. Köszönöm mindenkinek a támogatását, segítségét és imáit, melyekkel az elmúlt időben családommal együtt engem is erősítettek.” Ezekkel a mondatokkal köszönte meg a volt NKA-alelnök, egykori óbudai polgármester, a fideszes Bús Balázs a Facebookon , hogy kiengedték a letartóztatásból. Bús a mellékelt képen magyarul és lengyelül is köszönetet mondott, illetve a szövegben Ámosz prófétától is idézett, a következőt: „Okos ember hallgat ebben az időben, mert gonosz idő ez! A jót keressétek, ne a rosszat, és akkor éltek; és veletek lesz az Úr, a Seregek Istene, úgy, amint mondtátok. Gyűlöljétek a rosszat, szeressétek a jót, állítsátok helyre az igazságot a kapuban.” Szombaton írtunk róla , hogy hazamehet Bús Balázs, a Telex információja szerint ugyanis az ügyészség a védői indítványnak helyt adva kezdeményezte, hogy szüntessék meg a Nemzeti Kulturális Alap (NKA) volt alelnökének letartóztatását és helyezzék bűnügyi felügyelet alá. Mivel a bíróságnak ilyenkor nincs mérlegelési lehetősége, el kellett rendelnie a letartóztatás megszüntetését. Információnkat Bús védője is megerősítette. Papp Gábor a Telexnek akkor még azt mondta, hogy az indítványt még csütörtökön adta be az ügyészség. „A bíróságnak ezt soron kívül kellett volna elbírálnia, ez azonban még pénteken sem történt meg” – mondta a védő. Bús posztja alapján azóta valóban szabadulhatott. Előzmények Az NKA volt alelnökét június 25-én helyezték letartóztatásba , amit aztán kétszer is meghosszabbítottak, legutóbb október 22-én. A döntést a bíróság akkor azzal indokolta, hogy a bűncselekmény megalapozott gyanúja, valamint a kényszerintézkedés különös okai változatlanul fennállnak, ezért a gyanúsított jelenlétének biztosítása és a bizonyítás megnehezítésének megakadályozása érdekében két hónappal – december 25-ig – hosszabbította meg a letartóztatást, így szinte biztos volt, hogy Bús Balázs a szentestét is a börtönben tölti. Az NKA volt alelnöke egy október 22-i keltezésű levélben üzent a börtönből. Ebben azt írta, négy hónapja tartják fogva, szerinte jogtalanul, hiszen sem a szökés, sem a bűnismétlés, sem az eljárás befolyásolásának veszélye nem áll fent. Arról is írt, hogy szerinte olyan vallomást várnak el tőle, amely ellentétes az igazsággal és a hitével. A politikus politikai koncepciós eljárás áldozatának nevezte magát, egyúttal Magyar Pétert is megvádolta azzal, hogy befolyásolni próbálja a hatóságokat. Bús először 2021-től 2024 elejéig dolgozott az NKA alelnökeként, majd 2024 őszétől töltötte be újra ezt a pozíciót, április végén – a botrány fokozódásával – aztán lemondott a posztjáról . A Nemzet Adó- és Vámhivatal (NAV) magánszemélyek feljelentése után indított nyomozást, mert a gyanú szerint az NKA döntéshozó testülete 2024 decemberétől a törvényeket és szabályokat durván megszegve 1079 db, összesen 17 milliárd forintot meghaladó összegű támogatásról döntött. Június 23-án aztán a NAV tömör közleményben számolt be arról , hogy az NKA-botránnyal összefüggésben hat személyt őrizetbe is vettek : Bús Balázst, az NKA volt alelnökét, az NKA-nál futó pályázatok lebonyolításával megbízott intézmény, a Nemzeti Kulturális Támogatáskezelő (NKTK) főigazgatóját és kabinetvezetőjét, valamint annak a kiemelt bizottságnak a három tagját is, akik a 17 milliárd forint kiosztásáról is döntöttek. Bús Balázst az NKA-ügyben különösen jelentős vagyoni hátrányt okozó hűtlen kezeléssel gyanúsítják, időközben azonban az úgynevezett óbudai korrupciós ügyben is gyanúsított lett . https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/rach.text: Racheta de croazieră rusească Kh-101, ale cărei fragmente au fost recuperate în apropierea localității Nowy Lipowiec, din voievodatul Lublin, în estul Poloniei, a fost fabricată în Rusia în ultimul trimestru al anului 2026 și a explodat în aer înainte de a atinge solul, a anunțat procurorul polonez Andrzej Boroń. Anchetatorii au examinat locul incidentului și au recuperat numeroase fragmente împrăștiate pe o suprafață extinsă, înaintea reuniunii Consiliului Nord-Atlantic (NAC), programată luni, la Bruxelles, în urma încălcării spațiului aerian polonez de către Rusia , vineri, relatează Kyiv Post . Racheta de croazieră rusească Kh-101, ale cărei resturi au fost descoperite în apropierea localității Nowy Lipowiec, din voievodatul Lublin, în estul Poloniei, a fost fabricată în Rusia în ultimul trimestru al anului 2026 și a explodat în aer înainte de a lovi solul, împrăștiind fragmente pe o suprafață extinsă, a anunțat procurorul polonez Andrzej Boroń, potrivit Polskie Radio. Vorbind în numele Parchetului din Lublin, Boroń a confirmat că anchetatorii polonezi au examinat zona impactului, au reconstituit traiectoria de zbor a rachetei și au recuperat numeroase fragmente pentru expertize criminalistice. „Cunoșteam traiectoria aproximativă de zbor. S-a stabilit că este vorba despre o rachetă de croazieră de fabricație rusească. Pot, de asemenea, să confirm că a fost fabricată în ultimul trimestru al acestui an”, a declarat Boroń. Potrivit procurorului, concluziile preliminare ale expertizelor indică faptul că focosul rachetei a explodat deasupra solului, ceea ce explică dispersarea fragmentelor pe o suprafață atât de mare. „Potrivit concluziilor preliminare, explozia s-a produs deasupra solului. Tocmai de aceea, fragmentele au fost împrăștiate pe o suprafață foarte extinsă. Examinarea fiecărui fragment descoperit la fața locului este în curs de desfășurare”, a adăugat Boroń. Descoperirea faptului că racheta de croazieră Kh-101, lansată din aer, fusese fabricată recent, între octombrie și noiembrie 2026, și utilizată la doar câteva săptămâni după ieșirea de pe linia de producție evidențiază capacitatea Moscovei de a continua fabricarea în serie a rachetelor, în pofida restricțiilor occidentale privind exporturile. Președintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski a avertizat în repetate rânduri aliații internaționali că forțele ruse utilizează rachete balistice și de croazieră fabricate recent, trimise pe front aproape imediat după ieșirea de pe liniile de asamblare. Liderul de la Kiev a cerut Uniunii Europene să adopte un al 22-lea pachet de sancțiuni puternice, care să vizeze fabricile din industria de apărare, furnizorii de componente și rețelele de contrabandă cu microelectronică. Racheta Kh-101 descoperită la Nowy Lipowiec a fost unul dintre cele trei obiecte aeriene rusești care au încălcat spațiul aerian al Poloniei în dimineața zilei de vineri, 20 noiembrie, în timpul unui bombardament masiv lansat de Rusia asupra vestului Ucrainei. Ministrul polonez al Apărării, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, a confirmat că, pe lângă racheta Kh-101 descoperită în apropiere de Nowy Lipowiec, o a doua rachetă de croazieră suspectată că ar fi fost de fabricație rusească a căzut la Rudnik nad Sanem, iar o dronă cu propulsie reactivă s-a prăbușit la Młodochów (Molodycz). Citește și: Aproape 5.000 de militari europeni se antrenează în Polonia pentru o posibilă misiune în Ucraina. Moscova acuză o escaladare Un pilot suedez aflat la bordul unui avion de luptă JAS 39 Gripen, care patrula spațiul aerian polonez, a primit autorizația NATO de a doborî presupusa rachetă Kh-101. Pilotul a decis însă să nu deschidă focul, deoarece condițiile meteorologice severe au împiedicat confirmarea vizuală și prin senzori optoelectronici a țintei. După o vizită urgentă la Varșovia, sâmbătă, 21 noiembrie, secretarul general al NATO, Mark Rutte , a promis că Alianța „va apăra fiecare centimetru din teritoriul Poloniei”. Rutte a precizat că generalul Alexus Grynkewich, comandantul suprem al forțelor aliate din Europa, analizează capacitatea de descurajare a NATO pentru a identifica eventualele vulnerabilități. Evaluarea are loc înaintea reuniunii Consiliului Nord-Atlantic, programată luni, la Bruxelles, unde Polonia va fi reprezentată de ministrul adjunct al Apărării, Paweł Zalewski. NAZARETH TWP., Pa. – A popular business known for its authentic Hungarian specialties is in search of a new home base in the Lehigh Valley. Mattie’s Strudel Haus, offering a wide variety of hand-crafted Hungarian strudels, has moved operations out of 299 Industrial Drive in Upper Nazareth Township, Owner Kelly Vlasics told 69 News on Monday. Vlasics is currently seeking a new permanent home for Mattie’s, but in the meantime, the business continues to sell strudels – available in sweet and savory varieties – via home delivery and stands at local farmers markets, including Easton, Nazareth and Saucon Valley. In the spring, Vlasics moved operations to the Upper Nazareth spot , the same property where she kicked off Mattie’s operations nine years prior to that. Increasing demand led her to relocate the business in 2020 to 126 W. Main St. in Bath, but parking issues and other factors led her to close that location in 2025. Now, Mattie’s has moved out of the Upper Nazareth location once again, this time due to instances of theft and other unfortunate circumstances, Vlasics said. “I can’t be worrying all day about my strudels walking out of the door,” Vlasics said. “It’s just a shame. So, now I’m looking for a safe place with good parking.” Mattie's Strudel Haus A new Mattie’s location has not yet been nailed down, but Vlasics is looking into possibly establishing the business’ new home base on her property in Moore Township. A decision has not yet been finalized, Vlasics said. “I’m hoping the third times a charm,” Vlasics said in regard to Mattie’s yet-to-be-determined new home. Vlasics has been making the Hungarian specialties since childhood, when she learned the culinary skills from her mother, Bonnie Vlasics, and late Hungarian grandmother and the business’s namesake, Matilda “Mattie” Vlasics. When preparing the strudels, Kelly and her team stretch the dough extremely thin by hand before filling it with homemade mixtures and fresh ingredients - including fruits and vegetables from local farms and orchards such as Bechdolt's Orchards in Lower Saucon Township and Twin Maple Farms in East Allen Township - and then rolling it by hand. Customers can choose from a wide array of strudel varieties, including breakfast delights, savory meals and sweet treats. Dozens of rotating selections include savory options such as cheesesteak, cabbage kielbasa, pastie, taco, Mediterranean and chicken bacon ranch; sweet selections such as apple crisp, blueberry crumb, cherry cheesecake and apple caramel toffee; and seasonal creations such as pork and sauerkraut with mashed potatoes, reuben, peach cobbler, strawberry rhubarb, pumpkin cheesecake and "Gobble" (turkey, mashed potatoes and more). The strudels are sold frozen, allowing individuals to bake them fresh for any event. Mattie's Strudel Haus Current 8- and 16-inch strudels, available for delivery or pick-up at markets, include bacon egg and cheese, sausage egg and cheese, chicken cheesesteak with onions and peppers, cheesesteak (plain or with onions and peppers), cabbage, apple, apple pecan walnut, apple caramel toffee, tart cherry, cherry cheesecake and pumpkin cheesecake. Customers also can purchase Mattie’s popular Gobble strudel, featuring slow-roasted turkey (white and dark meat), homemade potato stuffing with sautéed celery, onions, bread, homemade mashed potatoes from Twin Maple Farms, corn, turkey gravy and cranberry sauce. Bite-sized strudels, $3 each, include apple, pumpkin, cannoli, blueberry, spinach artichoke, and jalapeño popper. Gift certificates are also available. Orders can be placed by calling or texting 215-301-1881. Vlasics announced the business’ transition on Mattie’s Strudel Haus’ Facebook page. “A huge, heartfelt thank you to everyone who has reached out with love and support during this time!” the announcement reads. “Tom and I are a bit worn out, but stepping away from that space has given us a clean slate to carefully select a new location conducive to all the business needs in a safe place for you to buy the beloved strudels. We planned making strudels way in advance and since they last 6 months in a freezer, we are ready to DELIVER these beauties to you.” For the latest Mattie's Strudel Haus news, including upcoming farmers market appearances and future operational updates, follow the business' Facebook page.
